title: Brief
description: What a client asks for. Deliberately short — a brief that specifies everything has already done the designing, and a brief that specifies nothing gives the corpus no standing. Anything absent is decided by the composer and reported as a decision, not smuggled in as a fact.

area_tolerance.description: Fraction either side of target that counts as a hit. Never negative — compose.py's area axis reads it as a denominator, and a negative one published a score of 902.8 "out of 100" before this bound existed.

bedrooms.description: Sleeping rooms including the principal chamber.

storeys.description: Leave unset and the composer picks from the massing.

massing.description: Force a skeleton, or leave unset and let style affinity choose.

must_have.description: Room type ids the client has explicitly asked for. The composer will not drop these.

site.description: Lot and settlement data beyond `context.lot_width_ft`/`lot_depth_ft`/`entrance_faces` (see schema/plan.schema.json's `site` for the full rationale). Set `lot_width_ft` in `context` as before; this object is where the composer reads setbacks, street bearing and the other WP-2.4 site fields it needs to filter partis and evaluate site-scope constraints.

household.description: Free text. Who lives here and how they use a house — the thing that decides whether the dining room gets built and never used.

candidates.description: How many contrasting plans to return.
